# Service Menu Build — The Forge

**Start with your revenue anchor, not your offerings.** Interview your top 5 paying members this week (30 mins each). Ask: "What made you sign up? What package are you on? Would you pay more for X?" This reveals what actually sells, not what you think should exist. Build your menu around those insights, not assumptions.

**Tier it ruthlessly — three tiers maximum.** Coaches need to sell fast; members need to decide fast. Structure: *Starter* (basic gym access), *Builder* (access + coaching sessions), *Elite* (priority booking + unlimited coaching). Price each so 60% of members are in the middle tier. That's your goldmine.

**Create a one-page visual for each audience.** Coaches get a *sales guide* (what to highlight, common objections, upsell pathways). Members get a *clear poster/digital card* (not a novel—three tiers, prices, three bullet-point benefits per tier). Laminate it. Put it at reception and email it out today.

**Lock in what's included operationally first.** Before you publish anything, confirm with your coaches: Can you actually deliver unlimited coaching in Elite? How many sessions per week is "included" in Builder sustainable? Price around reality, not wishful thinking.

**Soft-launch to existing members this week.** Send an email: "We've streamlined our offerings—see where you sit and what's next." Track which tier people choose; that data is gold for refinement.

What's your current rough tier structure?

## REVENUE — CRITICAL ISSUE: MEMBER QUALITY & PRICING COLLAPSE

• **Rev/member has tanked from £145 (July) to £106 (October).** You've added 31 net members (+26%) but revenue per head fell 27%. This signals either heavy discounting on new joiners, or a shift to lower-tier memberships. **Action:** Audit your current pricing tiers and new-member acquisition offers in TeamUp. If new cohorts are on trial/introductory rates, accelerate them to full price or lose margin permanently. Benchmark: you should be targeting £130+ per member/month minimum.

• **September spike (£22k) wasn't repeatable.** October dropped 19% week-on-week despite *higher* active members (167 vs 159). **Action:** Pull September's class attendance data — what drove it (summer retention boost, class schedule change, promo)? Replicate immediately in Nov–Dec.

• **Churn in May was 12.8% — double your normal rate.** Post-relocation disruption likely. Now stable at 3–6%, which is healthy. **But:** you're acquiring members faster than revenue grows, meaning discount or downgrade bias. **Action:** Stop volume-chasing. Tighten new-member onboarding to Premium tier (or add mandatory add-ons: PT sessions, nutrition coaching, merchandise) to restore £140+ ARPU.

• **No upsell revenue visible.** A 167-member gym should generate £2–4k/month in class packs, PT, apparel, supplements. **Action:** Launch a simple retail line (resistance bands, water bottles, protein) or block-book PT sessions (6-week courses at £300–500 each). Low friction, high margin.

---
